entry.title: PasRISCV RISC-V Emulator Enables In-Game Linux for SEEDS
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | againstallodds.games | discussion | hacker news

PasRISCV is an open-source RISC-V 64-bit emulator written in Object Pascal that provides a fully emulated Alpine Linux system for the game SEEDS. The system simulates a complete virtual machine—including CPU, memory, and I/O—allowing native Linux binaries to run on a host machine.

The emulator features a hybrid CPU model using an interpreter and a tracing JIT compiler for x86-64 hosts and supports RVA23 and SMP. Integration is handled via Linux Virtual Sockets (vsock) to facilitate high-speed communication between the game engine and the guest system.

entry.title: Timur Kristóf Details AMDGPU Driver Enhancements for Legacy AMD GPUs
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | phoronix.com | source | hacker news

Timur Kristóf of Valve's Linux graphics driver team has presented enhancements to the AMDGPU kernel driver designed for legacy AMD GCN 1.0/1.1 era graphics cards and APUs. This work facilitates the transition of older hardware from the legacy Radeon driver to the modern AMDGPU stack, enabling support for the RADV Vulkan driver and addressing various display and power management defects.

These enhancements, which include soft reset support, aim to maintain the viability of aging hardware for Linux gaming and other tasks. The effort addresses driver gaps for decade-old silicon, building on performance improvements previously observed in the Linux 6.19 kernel.

entry.title: AI Models Simulate Oil Painting Using Code and Physics-Based Simulations
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | stillwet.art | hacker news

The Stillwet project explores AI agents acting as painters within a physics-based simulation of oil paint on linen. Rather than using generative image models, these agents write code to interact with virtual tools, including bristle brushes, wet paint, and layered glazes.

The experiments involve models such as Claude and Gemini attempting to emulate the styles of artists like Edward Hopper and Caspar David Friedrich. Observations include emergent behaviors such as a recurring preference for "dusk" lighting and instances where different models independently produced similar compositions.

entry.title: OpenDLSS-NR Reimplements NVIDIA DLSS 5 Neural Rendering in Vulkan
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | github.com | hacker news

OpenDLSS-NR is a Vulkan-based reimplementation of NVIDIA's DLSS 5 Neural Rendering network, designed to be bit-exact to the original. The implementation utilizes a 71-block Swin/ViT network running in FP8 on tensor cores, with intermediates matching the original byte for byte across all 75 block boundaries.

The project includes a WebGPU implementation for browsers and a demo utilizing the Filament renderer. Users must provide their own proprietary model weights to run the implementation on Windows machines equipped with NVIDIA Ada architecture GPUs or newer.

entry.title: Factorio Quality Upcycling: Mathematical Model and Calculator
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | exyr.org | hacker news

Mathematical modeling using transition matrices and linear equations allows for the calculation of quality transitions in the *Factorio: Space Age* expansion. This approach specifically addresses "washing" (pure recycling loops) and "upcycling" (crafting-recycling cycles) to predict how items move through different quality tiers.

An online calculator tool is provided to help players forecast resource consumption and output rates for high-quality items. The model incorporates variables such as module probabilities, recycling ingredient returns, and recipe productivity bonuses.

entry.title: Valve to Transition Steam's Discounts and Events Tab to Personalized Algorithms
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Valve is transitioning Steam's "Discounts and Events" tab from a manual, calendar-based system to an algorithm-driven recommendation engine. This shift aims to increase game discoverability by presenting personalized content tailored to individual users. Preliminary testing showed the personalized model displayed ten times more games daily, which increased store page visits, wishlists, and cart additions.

The transition is expected to reach full implementation by early 2027, following a current pause on new manual curated placements. The change is intended to benefit smaller developers by reducing the need for manual scheduling or direct curation by Valve staff. Industry feedback suggests the shift can drive significant traffic to niche titles that previously had minimal visibility on the curated page.

entry.title: Mikael Kasurinen Explains Decision to Avoid Yellow Paint in Control Resonant
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Following the launch of Remedy Entertainment's Control Resonant, director Mikael Kasurinen explained the studio's decision to eschew common visual shorthand for player guidance in favor of organic environmental cues. This design choice aims to enhance player agency, ensuring players feel they have discovered paths themselves rather than following dictated routes. In the game's gravity-shifting Manhattan, navigation is guided by subtle elements like wind and rain direction instead of explicit color-coded markers.

The choice addresses industry-wide debate over "handholding" mechanics intended to reduce player frustration. Kasurinen argues that excessive signposting can disrupt the horror-inspired theme of interpreting an unknowable reality. By relying on environmental subtlety, the developers aim to make navigation an active part of the player experience.

The shift follows a period where developers struggled to balance rapid content production with the heavy maintenance required for a live-service title. Grøndal emphasized that creating frameworks for work-life balance is essential to retaining the creative talent necessary for the game's long-term success.
